panels.rationale: Coronal CT of the hand in a patient with clinically suspected acute compartment syndrome of the hand after a parrot bite; caption and in-text state soft tissue swelling of the dorsal hand without bony abnormality, marked by a red arrow. The patient was evaluated by the hand surgeon at 20:15 hours and taken immediately to the operating room. panels.rationale: Single-panel axial MRI of a human patient's right lower extremity from a case report titled 'Acute compartment syndrome resultant from alcohol abuse.' The caption and in-text state the MRI shows a large hematoma in the superficial posterior compartment (intermuscular fascial plane between the medial head of gastrocnemius and soleus) in a patient whose compartment pressures (72/74 mmHg) confirmed acute compartment syndrome. The image is a photograph of the imaging monitor, slightly degraded but interpretable; the visible abnormality is a large compartmental fluid collection with surrounding soft-tissue swelling, which supports the compartment pathology in this ACS case. No finding in the vocabulary precisely matches a compartment hematoma, so it is recorded as a proposed finding; disease attribution rests on the case-specific captioned manifestation plus the ACS-focused article title.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Axial CT of the left leg shows diffuse deep posterior compartment edema and swelling in a patient with acute compartment syndrome following calf kicks; the finding supports ACS, though the available finding key specifies MRI. B: Sagittal CT of the left leg shows diffuse deep posterior compartment edema and swelling in a patient with acute compartment syndrome following calf kicks; the finding supports ACS, though the available finding key specifies MRI.

Journal of functional morphology and kinesiology 2026. doi:10.3390/jfmk11020206. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Imaging (axial (A) and sagittal (B) views) revealed diffuse edema of the left leg with pronounced swelling predominantly involving the deep posterior compartment. The yellow arrows indicate the hematoma. A well-circumscribed intramuscular hematoma measuring approximately 4.5 × 4.5 cm was identified within the left soleus muscle. Following intravenous contrast administration, there was no evidence of active arterial bleeding or contrast extravasation. Mild focal compression of the posterior tibial artery was observed at its mid-portion, while arterial flow and distal vessel patency remained preserved.
in_text_mentions: Given the progressive onset of symptoms following relatively minor trauma, with no clinical signs of bone lesion, laxity, or articular instability, CT angiography was performed because of the atypical mechanism of injury and concern for an underlying vascular lesion or active bleeding source. Imaging demonstrated diffuse edema predominantly involving the deep posterior compartment of the left leg, associated with a large intramuscular hematoma within the left soleus muscle measuring approximately 4.5 × 4.5 cm (Figure 2). No active arterial extravasation was identified.
